SharedProducer.bounds: Two concurrent waiters, one shared or two separate producers, one replacement; transport and immutable domains; five contexts; immutable registry limit 1 or 2 with unit-weight producers. The admission bound includes unfinished finalizers, not independent overflow reads. Equality abstracts the complete request or current-resource identity.
SharedProducer.scope: Transport coalescers are service local. Exact current resource bytes may share across standard Node SDK runtimes in one process only after each caller qualifies its current owner and File descriptor. The producer owns an independent read-only transport Scope and no caller Store. The key includes the real Store root, detached credential/origin/version/scheduling identity, library, current owner/content descriptor and read policy. Custom transports without a detached context and calls with RequestBudget bypass this sharing. Completed values are not retained. Dependency coverage is limited to pending Cache reference counting and current-entry cleanup.

RequestAdmission.bounds: One logical request and its retry chain under a supplied operation allowance: two admitted attempts, four clock ticks, short/long queue window and one-tick attempt timer; read and mutating variants. Success is terminal, so this is not a model of a multi-request current writer invocation.
RequestAdmission.scope: Covers cooldown/admission ordering, queue and operation deadlines, attempt count and timeout, permit/lease ownership and rejection versus unknown-write retry. SQL claims are abstract atomic decisions. No proof of SQLite driver/crash behavior, arbitrary clocks, fairness, all quota scopes, cross-machine scheduling, byte arithmetic or current writer lifecycle. The mandatory current invocation wrapper and byte/nesting behavior are implementation regressions listed separately below.

unmodeled_bindings.name: current_invocation_http_budget
unmodeled_bindings.scope: One outer current invocation installs defaults of 1000 HTTP requests, 512 MiB payload bytes and 600000 ms; explicit outer limits may override them. Nested work inherits the same identity, counters and permit and rejects changed limits. Notion requests, provider downloads and multipart payloads share accounting; repeated wrapping does not double charge. Limits are copied and frozen, and first exhaustion prevents later admission, including attention or cleanup. Transport-owned deadlines retain unknown-write semantics. A later resume invocation gets a fresh allowance. The real HTTP regression covers mixed transports, byte exhaustion, current ZIP wire limits, interrupted writer behavior and exact-input resume. Neither TLA module enumerates these byte, wrapper, multipart, multi-step writer, ready/applying/attention, pending-intent or recovery states.

unmodeled_bindings.name: operation_subprocess_environment_and_group_cleanup
unmodeled_bindings.scope: SDK options.env is a complete operation snapshot used by ConfigProvider and inherited child processes; explicit command environments retain their policy and safe Git scrub wins. Concurrent callers do not mutate process.env. Public consume wiring is exercised against owned loopback metadata and actual Git shims, with no real origin fetch. POSIX cancellation owns a process group and waits for leader and descendants; SIGTERM-resistant descendants are force-killed after the existing two-second bound. The frozen platform implementation is bound by exact bytes, not claimed as fully verified. Bun and Node process tests are distinct from external Git/auth/network performance. RequestEngine finite variables do not model environment maps, OS groups, signals, Git wire bytes, credential waits, Source cold success, or ordinary Pi deadlines.
